claims.text: Brand was the son of King Bain and grandson of Bard the Bowman who had killed the dragon Smaug.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "Many Meetings"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Fire and Water"

claims.text: He became the king of Dale and by he had extended the realm of Dale far south and east of Esgaroth.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "Many Meetings"

claims.text: At the Council of Elrond the dwarf Glóin reported that a year earlier (in ) a messenger from Mordor had come to speak to Dáin. He also said that messengers had spoken to King Brand and that he was afraid, for war appeared to be gathering on his eastern borders.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "The Council of Elrond"

claims.text: However, when news of Sauron's defeat came his northern army was dismayed with his son (and Dáin's son, Thorin) breaking the siege. King Brand was succeeded by his son, Bard II.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Great Years"
